about: A lane's signed batch carries the places its own lines are meant for: bound sign --place p writes # place p above the lines, and the accept that lands the cycle routes that file's own lines to those places only, among the ones its signer covers. A batch naming no place keeps the accept's --place. A place that is not one of the tree's refuses the act by name. bound release <folder> prints the release digest of a folder as the host names what it lays, so a script names a release without importing the instrument.

cases.name: bound release over the laid obligations 0.3.3 and over the published folder obligations-release, on a copy at 315
cases.answer: RELEASE sha256:b3dab950… for both, the digest the lay's mark and receipt carry

cases.name: a batch signed with --place bound, accepted with no --place
cases.landed: its own line in bound/TARGET.bound only

cases.name: the same batch naming # place nowhere
cases.answer: REFUSE·place: nowhere is no place of the tree

red was: a cycle whose own lines went wherever their signer was admitted
